description: Renderer selection. A renderer decides how approved product truth is turned into a repository; it never decides what the product is. Every renderer consumes the same Manifest, KnowledgePack, Composition, PageSpec/SectionSpec, DesignSystemSpec, BrandSpec, ArtDirectionPlan, ResponsiveCompositionPlan, MotionContract and Presentation Registry. Selection is a pure function of the project type and the capabilities the manifest enables, so the same approved truth always reaches the same renderer.

static-content.label: Static / content
static-content.purpose: Public websites whose value is the content, not the session. Every route is a real document generated at build time; client code exists only where a component genuinely needs it.

application.label: Application
application.purpose: Products that are worked in rather than read. State, session and interaction are the product, so the client runtime is the point rather than a cost.

capabilityOverrides.reason: The manifest enables a capability that is an authenticated or stateful application area rather than a page. A public site with a real application inside it is an application, and rendering it statically would ship a login as a document.

rules: A renderer renders decisions. It introduces no composer, product schema, content model, Design Contract, brand system, art-direction system, presentation authority or source/provenance model of its own.
Project type selects the default renderer. A capability override may only move a project to a renderer that can carry the capability; it never moves one away from a renderer that already can.
An override is recorded on the generated project, with its reason, so a build that did not use its project type's default can say why.
A combination no renderer supports fails closed. A recipe, adapter or presentation with no implementation for the selected renderer is an error, never a silent substitution.
Selection never reads a prompt, a model or free text. Only the project type and the enabled modules decide.
